verdict.reasoning:
King County hosts (aqua/info/www5/www.kingcounty.gov, web.archive.org, app.leg.wa.gov) are egress-blocked from this sandbox, so I could not probe the URL or headers directly. Instead I (1) found ~85 GitHub files across many independent repos (Flatiron/learn-co curricula, hoffm386, aspotter99, varunr89, BraPil, zz85, PHSKC-APDE, psrc) that download exactly https://aqua.kingcounty.gov/extranet/assessor/Residential%20Building.zip and extract EXTR_ResBldg.csv; and (2) downloaded a full copy of the file that BraPil's repo ships (data/king_county/EXTR_ResBldg.csv.gz, gzip header says original name EXTR_ResBldg.csv, mtime 2025-12-09, 154,059,942 bytes) and inspected it in an isolated directory with python -I.

Direct inspection of that Dec-2025 vintage confirms the claim's substance: 50 columns with exactly the header claimed (Major, Minor, BldgNbr, NbrLivingUnits, Address, ..., ZipCode, Stories, BldgGrade, SqFt1stFloor/SqFt2ndFloor/SqFtUpperFloor, SqFtTotLiving, SqFtTotBasement, Bedrooms, BathHalfCount/Bath3qtrCount/BathFullCount, YrBuilt, YrRenovated, Condition, ...); no owner/taxpayer name fields. 531,978 rows / 524,122 distinct PINs (claim says 533,734 / 525,498 for the Oct-2026 vintage; ~1,750 rows more after 10 months is consistent with 2,852 buildings dated 2025 in this copy). YrBuilt: min nonzero = 1894 (exactly 1 row), nothing 1895-1899, 2,032 rows at 1900 (claim: 2,010), max 2025; YrRenovated is 0 for 504,799 rows (nonzero min 1914). Major is always 6 chars and Minor always 4 chars; values are space-padded (StreetName padded in 531,694 rows, Address in 55,591). Stories is decimal (1.5, 2.5 ...). File size 154.06 MB CSV vs claimed 154.6 MB; 17.9 MB gz vs claimed 21.7 MB zip; 2019 vintage per hoffm386 notebook was 149.1 MB CSV / 24.6 MB zipped. The same column list appears independently in thoughtfulml's load_data.sql and uncheckederror/RealProperty's C# model.

CORS: cannot be probed from here, but zz85/random-sketches README independently states for aqua.kingcounty.gov/extranet/assessor/*.zip: "No CORS, so bundled by fetch_data.js" - consistent with build-time-only use. Refresh cadence (~weekly) is reported only by a third party (localscape.property: "King County Assessor data tables are refreshed weekly"); data.gov says "periodically"; unverified but not contradicted.

Terms: web-search snippets of kingcounty.gov/About/dataTermsOfUse.aspx confirm "King County grants you a limited, revocable license to use, reproduce, and redistribute the Data" and the legend "Data provided by permission of King County"; snippets of info.kingcounty.gov/assessor/DataDownload/default.aspx confirm the RCW 42.56.070(9) 'lists of individuals for commercial purposes' acknowledgement. A public, non-commercial hobby site citing 'King County Assessor' is compatible. Caveats (not refutations) are listed in corrected_facts.

Net: every load-bearing part of the claim (URL, file name, fields incl. YrBuilt/YrRenovated, PIN construction, padding, build-time-only, no API key, no names, 1894 floor with 1900 cluster, size, terms) is confirmed by direct inspection or multiple independent sources; the only unverifiable items are the exact Oct-2026 counts/Last-Modified and the live ACAO header, and those are consistent with the evidence. Not refuted.
verdict.corrected_facts: Minor corrections from direct inspection of the 2025-12-09 extract (531,978 rows): (1) BldgGrade is not strictly 1-13: code 0 (Unknown, 1 row) and code 20 ('Exceptional Properties', 12 rows) also occur - King County GIS catalog and uncheckederror/RealProperty confirm 0=Unknown, 1 Cabin ... 13 Mansion, 20 Exceptional Properties. (2) Condition is 1-5 but code 0 occurs (2 rows). (3) NbrLivingUnits is not confined to 1-3: 803 rows have 4 and 1 row has 12 (plus 1 row of 0); treat as '1-4'. (4) 'Nothing before 1894' should read 'nothing before 1894 except 2 rows with YrBuilt=0 (unknown)'; the 1900 cluster was 2,032 rows in Dec 2025. (5) Stories has a handful of junk values (0, 1.2, 1816) - validate before use. (6) 'The file is latin1': the Dec-2025 ResBldg file contains zero bytes >= 0x80 (pure ASCII), so reading it as UTF-8 also works; latin1 is still the safe choice because sibling extracts (EXTR_RPSale, EXTR_Parcel) do contain non-ASCII bytes and several repos read ResBldg with encoding='latin1'/'ISO-8859-1'. (7) Major/Minor already arrive zero-padded as 6- and 4-character quoted strings; the padding only gets lost if a parser coerces them to integers. (8) RCW 42.56.070's lists-of-individuals clause is currently subsection (8); King County's page still cites (9) - cite the statute without the subsection number, or as (8). (9) Terms nuance: the open-data terms (revocable license to use/reproduce/redistribute + legend) are the permissive ones; the Assessor eSales site and countywide web terms restrict redistribution/commercial exploitation of 'web content' without written permission, and the GIS catalog says the GIS copy (resbldg_extr) is 'not authoritative' and its digital products may not be redistributed without permission - so cite the extranet CSV, show the 'Data provided by permission of King County' legend, and keep the site non-commercial. (10) Row counts: 531,978 rows / 524,122 PINs as of 2025-12-09; the claimed 533,734 / 525,498 for 2026-10-01 is plausible but was not independently verified, nor was the Last-Modified date or the live absence of an ACAO header. (11) Refresh cadence: 'weekly' comes from a third party (localscape.property); data.gov describes King County assessor datasets as updated 'periodically'.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to break the claim on five fronts and it held on all the ones that matter.

1. Does the URL exist? Yes. Four unrelated public GitHub projects construct and download this exact URL: psrc/parcels (AssessorToDb.py: url_base 'https://aqua.kingcounty.gov/extranet/assessor/' + 'Commercial Building.zip', spaces to %20, fetched with a bare requests.get), uncheckederror/RealProperty (appsettings.json: "CommericalBuilding": "https://aqua.kingcounty.gov/extranet/assessor/Commercial%20Building.zip"), PHSKC-APDE/kcparcelpop (prepare_parcel_data.R cites the URL and reads EXTR_CommBldg.csv), and chrico7/data515_project (kc_real_estate.py lists 'Commercial%20Building' among 24 valid names on the DataDownload page and reads the zip straight into pandas). The repo's own live probe (docs/WA-PROBES.md, commit eb6f073, 2026-10-07) also got the file. kingcounty.gov hosts are egress-blocked from this sandbox, so the 403 I got is not evidence either way.

2. Does it carry the claimed fields, especially YrBuilt/EffYr? Yes. RealProperty's CsvHelper model maps CSV columns 0-25 as: Major, Minor, BldgNbr, NbrBldgs, Address, BuildingNumber, Fraction, DirectionPrefix, StreetName, StreetType, DirectionSuffix, ZipCode, NbrStories, PredominantUse, Shape, ConstrClass, BldgQuality, BldgDescr, BldgGrossSqFt, BldgNetSqFt, YrBuilt, EffYr, PcntComplete, HeatingSystem, Sprinklers, Elevators. That is byte-for-byte the header in the repo probe and a superset of the claim's list. PSRC's urbansim SQL selects bldgnbr, nbrstories, predominantuse, bldgquality, bldggrosssqft, bldgnetsqft, yrbuilt from extr_commbldg; brshallo/sps-elem-data aggregates YrBuilt and EffYr weighted by BldgNetSqFt from EXTR_CommBldg.csv. The companion tables are real too: RealProperty lists EXTR_CommBldgSection.csv (SectionNbr, SectionUse, NbrStories, StoryHeight, GrossSqFt, NetSqFt, SectionDescr) and EXTR_CommBldgFeature.csv (FeatureType, GrossSqFt, NetSqFt), and PSRC's SQL indexes extr_commbldgsection / extr_commbldgfeature.

3. Usable as claimed (build-time, no CORS, no key)? Yes. Every consumer is server-side; none sends credentials. zz85/random-sketches documents the same host independently: "aqua.kingcounty.gov/extranet/assessor/*.zip ... No CORS, so bundled by fetch_data.js". The repo probe saw no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. PSRC reads the CSVs as ISO-8859-1, matching the latin1 note on the residential extract.

4. Terms compatible with a public hobby site? Yes, with care. Search snippets of the DataDownload page confirm its only gate is the acknowledgment "I have requested copies of the public records of the Assessor's Property Information Files. I understand that Washington State law, RCW 42.56.070(9), prohibits the use of lists of individuals for 'commercial purposes.'" This extract is building characteristics with no person names (King County even ships the account file as EXTR_RPAcct_NoName.csv), so it is not a list of individuals and a non-commercial site is doubly clear. King County's open-data terms (dataTermsOfUse.aspx) grant a limited, revocable license to use, reproduce and redistribute with the legend "Data provided by permission of King County"; those terms formally cover data.kingcounty.gov and the opendata.arcgis.com sites rather than aqua.kingcounty.gov, but adopting the legend costs nothing.

5. What I could NOT verify: the exact figures (41,836 rows, 31,407 PINs, 2 rows in the 1880s, 3.7 MB, Last-Modified 2026-10-03) come only from the repo's live probe; no external source states a row count. Weekly refresh is corroborated by localscape.property ("King County Assessor data tables are refreshed weekly"). The second evidence URL, www5.kingcounty.gov/sdc/?Layer=commbldg_extr, is unreachable from here, has zero GitHub hits, and is not indexed anywhere I could find, so it is unconfirmed; KCGIS catalog records usually carry boilerplate that digital products "may not be reproduced or redistributed ... without the express written authorization of King County", which argues for publishing only derived per-parcel facts with attribution rather than mirroring the raw CSV. One naming wrinkle: PSRC's 2023 urbansim scripts read "EXTR_CommBldg2.csv", but that path is an internal PSRC processing share; PSRC's own assessor-housing-estimates, RealProperty (2022), kcparcelpop and the 2026 probe all use EXTR_CommBldg.csv, so match the name loosely rather than hard-coding it.

Net: existence, fields, access method and terms are all independently corroborated; only the precise counts and one evidence URL rest on the in-repo probe. Not refuted.
verdict.corrected_facts:
- RCW citation: the list-of-individuals clause is now RCW 42.56.070(8) (renumbered around 2017); King County's page still prints "(9)". Quote the page as-is but cite the statute as 42.56.070(8).
- Full header has 26 columns, not the 18 the claim lists: it also carries BuildingNumber, Fraction, DirectionPrefix, StreetName, StreetType, DirectionSuffix, ZipCode and HeatingSystem.
- Do not hard-code the CSV name inside the zip; match /^EXTR_CommBldg2?\.csv$/i (PSRC's 2023 pipeline saw a "2"-suffixed copy; every direct download seen names it EXTR_CommBldg.csv).
- Read as latin1 (ISO-8859-1) and trim space-padded values, as PSRC does.
- Evidence URL www5.kingcounty.gov/sdc/?Layer=commbldg_extr is unverified from this sandbox and KCGIS catalog records normally forbid redistributing the raw product without written authorization; publish only derived per-PIN facts and add the open-data legend "Data provided by permission of King County" alongside "King County Assessor".
- Row counts, 1880s rows, zip size and Last-Modified date are sourced solely from the repo's 2026-10-07 live probe (docs/WA-PROBES.md); treat them as a snapshot, not a documented constant (file refreshes weekly).

gaps: 1) No open dataset anywhere in Washington gives a FIRST OWNER. The free proxies are PlatName/PlatLot/PlatBlock from the King County Parcel extract (the subdivider's name is usually in the plat name), Seattle's Historical Sites survey (builder/architect, 5,000+ properties, link-out only, no API), the 517 Seattle Landmarks, Wikidata/Wikipedia for notable buildings, and the 1937-1972 assessor record cards (link-out). Plat RECORDING DATES are not in any extract: King County's platfile_extr is 'Not Public', the Recorder's online index starts 1976, and the 1853-1975 General Recordings Index is offline at King County Archives (the Digital Archives collection 'King County Recorder, Plats and Surveys, 1870-Present' is a link-out). 2) Assessor data describes the CURRENT structure only: nothing before 1894 in King County, no demolished buildings, and a 1900 placeholder year (2,010 King rows; Garfield High shows 1900 in PARCEL_GEO). For 'what stood here in 1910/1950' the house ring must fall back to Sanborn sheets (LOC), OHM building ways, record cards and photos. Year built also differs by county semantics (Pierce has year_built AND adjusted_year_built; Thurston YEAR_BUILT vs EFF_YR_BUI; King YrBuilt vs YrRenovated; Seattle PARCEL_GEO is the NEWEST building). Always say 'the assessor records…' and link the DATA_LINK page. 3) Statewide 'Current Parcels' has NO year built and no building fields beyond VALUE_BLDG; its license lets single-parcel display but says some counties restrict reuse to state business, so never bulk-copy it. 4) Field-level verification is still missing for every county-hosted ArcGIS server because the sandbox blocks all *.wa.gov/*.county hosts: Whatcom layer 1, Skagit Tax_Parcels, Yakima ParcelAnalysis table, Benton Parcels_and_Assess, Clallam Parcel_Published_Public, Island Geocortex/Base, Spokane features_info vs curr_year_info, Clark PropImprvVw column names, Kitsap Dwellings.txt header, the Snohomish Improvement Records download URL, and the DAHP HPI schema. Each needs one ?f=pjson or header read from a machine with normal egress (a GitHub Actions runner will do). CORS is unverified for county-hosted servers (ArcGIS Server allows all origins by default; Island reflects Origin; AGOL-hosted services send *). 5) Owner/taxpayer names leak onto several public layers (Snohomish OWNERNAME/TAXPRNAME, Island taxpayer, Skagit OwnerName, Thurston mailing address). The site should never request or display them; several county terms and RCW 42.56.070(9) forbid commercial lists of individuals, and Spokane's hosted parcels are CC BY-NC-SA. 6) Census-style 'who lived here' data (city directories, census sheets) is out of scope for open APIs; Seattle city directories 1938+ are offline at Seattle Public Library/Archives. 7) The King County extracts encode condo units as Minor != 0000 under a complex Major and unplatted land as Minor 9xxx; the build script must handle both or ~15% of PIN lookups will miss. 8) Kitsap/Thurston/Pierce/Snohomish bulk files each have a different delimiter, key (rp_acct_id, PARCEL_NO 11-digit, parcel_number 10-char, PARCEL_ID 14-digit) and update rhythm, so every added county is a bespoke parser; Regrid's coverage figures (Thurston 85%, Benton 87%, Snohomish 86%, Whatcom 78%, Kitsap 76%, Yakima 76%, Skagit 63%, Clallam 57%) are a good proxy for how complete each county's year built will be.
recommendation: SEATTLE / KING COUNTY: use the BUILD-TIME path. A GitHub Actions job (weekly cron, ~2 minutes, ~57 MB of downloads) fetches Residential Building, Commercial Building, Parcel (+ Apartment Complex and Condo Complex) from aqua.kingcounty.gov, stream-parses the latin1 CSVs, trims padded values, and writes sharded JSON keyed by PIN: file = data/kc/<first 3 digits of Major>.json (at most 1,000 files), each holding {majors: {<Major>: [platName, platBlockOfComplexYrBuilt...]}, pins: {<Minor>: [yrBuiltOldest, yrBuiltNewest, yrRenovated, stories*10, sqftLiving, grade, condition, nBldgs, presentUseCode, platLot, platBlock]}}. With ~630k parcels at ~40 bytes per row that is ~25 MB of JSON in the repo (~7 MB gzipped on the wire in total) and an average shard of ~25 KB raw / ~7 KB gzipped, i.e. one small request per visit on a phone; the script should split any hot prefix (unplatted section-based Majors such as 092503 carry hundreds of 9xxx Minors) to a 4-digit prefix when a file exceeds ~150 KB, and commit only changed shards so weekly diffs stay small. Runtime: geocode (Photon/Nominatim) -> point query on KCGIS KingCo_PropertyInfo/MapServer/2 (PIN, ADDR, PROPTYPE, PREUSE, polygon) -> fetch the shard -> pins[minor] or, if absent, majors[major] (condo/apartment complex) -> render. Inside Seattle also query PARCEL_GEO (YR_BUILT_MAX, YR_RENOV_MAX, NR_STORIES_MAX, BLDG_DESC, LANDMARK) as a cross-check and as the fallback if the shard is missing; disagreements (oldest vs newest building, 1900 placeholder) should be shown honestly ('assessor records 1925; newest structure 1998'). The same shard gives the BLOCK ring for free: all Minors of a Major are the lots of one plat, so 'most houses in <PlatName> were built in the 1920s' is a one-line aggregation with no extra fetch. Link out from the house ring to the Assessor's eReal Property page (PIN), Seattle Historical Sites (address), and the 1937-1972 record cards. Do NOT choose the pure runtime path for year built in King County: the only CORS source with year built is Seattle-only, and the KC server has none. REST OF WASHINGTON (realistic statement): at runtime, query the statewide Current Parcels FeatureServer (fallback: the DNR mirror) by point and show parcel number, situs address, DOR land-use description, 'building value > 0 = there is a structure here', the per-county file date, and a 'See the county assessor's record (year built, buildings)' link built from DATA_LINK; this works for all 39 counties today with zero build work. Add live year built for Thurston County from Thurston_Parcels (YEAR_BUILT, EFF_YR_BUI, RES_QUAL, RES_COND) once a CORS probe confirms it. Phase 2, only if friends outside King County ask: extend the same build-time shard format (keyed by the county's own parcel number, matched to ORIG_PARCEL_ID from the statewide layer) with Pierce (improvement_builtas.zip: year_built, adjusted_year_built, stories, square feet; weekly pipe text), Snohomish (Improvement Records: yrbuilt, stories, finsize) and Kitsap (Dwellings.txt YEAR_BUILT via rp_acct_id), which together with King and Thurston cover roughly 60% of Washington's population; Spokane and Clark are feasible later from their bulk text bundles once a column check is done. Treat Whatcom, Skagit, Yakima, Benton, Clallam and Island as 'parcel + link-out' until their layers are probed. Policy for every source: attribute the county assessor and the state Geospatial Program, show an 'as of' date, never display owner/taxpayer names, and keep Spokane-derived data non-commercial and share-alike.

verdict.reasoning:
Could not reach services.arcgis.com, catalog.data.gov, hub.arcgis.com, geo.btaa.org or clerk.seattle.gov from the sandbox (egress proxy blocks them), so no live probe was possible; the web-search budget was also exhausted after two queries. The claim was instead cross-checked against sources independent of the repo's own probe (docs/WA-PROBES.md, 2026-10-07):

EXISTENCE: the exact URL https://services.arcgis.com/ZOyb2t4B0UYuYNYH/arcgis/rest/services/nma_nhoods_sub/FeatureServer/0 is indexed by the search engine as a live page titled "Name: nma_nhoods_sub". Six unrelated GitHub projects fetch it anonymously (autowandr vendored a copy on 2026-05-08 noting the hub page reported a 2026-04-20 data update; civicmapper, pick-app, seattle-fire-and-crime, algorithmic-transit-design). data.gov carries both "Neighborhood Map Atlas Neighborhoods" and "Neighborhood Map Atlas Districts" records pointing at this service.

FIELDS AND COUNTS: a third-party GeoJSON copy (raceconditionrunning.github.io/routes/neighborhoods.geojson) contains exactly 94 Seattle features whose properties are exactly OBJECTID, L_HOOD, S_HOOD, S_HOOD_ALT_NAMES, Shape__Area, Shape__Length; 20 distinct L_HOOD values (Ballard, Beacon Hill, Capitol Hill, Cascade, Central Area, Delridge, Downtown, Greater Duwamish, Interbay, Lake City, Magnolia, North Central, Northeast, Northgate, Northwest, Queen Anne, Rainier Valley, Seward Park, University District, West Seattle); no date/year fields; "Lower Queen Anne" alt names "Uptown, Seattle Center" matches the repo probe's Space Needle result. autowandr's PROVENANCE.md independently counted 94 with jq and lists the same key properties; pick-app's code says "all 94 shapes"; civicmapper's script documents nma_nhoods_main/FeatureServer/0 as the dissolved 20-district layer, "public, no token".

LICENSE/TERMS: the City's own FGDC metadata for cityclerk_nma_nhoods_main (vendored in several repos) has accconst "Public." and useconst beginning "PDDL | This item is meant for public access and use. The City of Seattle makes no representation or warranty as to its accuracy", and adds that the City "reserve[s] the right to alter, suspend, re-host, or retire this service at any time and without notice". The abstract calls it "an unofficial delineation of neighborhood boundaries used by the City Clerks Office" and says the names/boundaries "are not intended to represent any official City of Seattle neighborhood map". data.gov's dataset record lists PDDL (the resource-level record says "other-license-specified", a harvest artifact, not a contradiction). PDDL is a public-domain dedication, so a public hobby site is fine; crediting City of Seattle / Seattle GeoData is courtesy, not a legal condition.

DATES: FGDC time period 2011-01-01, alt names supplemented in 2020, metadata date 2020-12-01; no per-feature dates. The claim's "present-day, undated boundaries" is accurate.

verdict.reasoning: Verified live against primary sources (the Seattle GeoData Hub search API, the ArcGIS Online item API at seattle.maps.arcgis.com, the Hub v3 dataset API and the services.arcgis.com REST endpoints all answered curl from this sandbox, with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on the Hub API and the FeatureServers). The Hub slug SeattleCityGIS::community-reporting-areas-3 resolves to item 23e2cd44d0b248c5ba6115eaee6df9cf, title "Community Reporting Areas", owner Planning_SeattleCityGIS, license PDDL-1.0, backed by https://services.arcgis.com/ZOyb2t4B0UYuYNYH/arcgis/rest/services/CITYPLAN_CRA/FeatureServer/43 (the service's only layer is id 43, named CITYPLAN.CRA; layer 0 does not exist, which explains the "layers=43" puzzle in the notes). Layer 43 fields: OBJECTID, CRA_NO, CRA_GRP, GEN_ALIAS, DETL_NAMES, NEIGHDIST, AREA_ACRES, AREA_SQMI, SE_ANNO_CAD_DATA (blob), DISPLAY_NAME, WATER, Shape__Area, Shape__Length. The layer description confirms the boundaries were updated to follow 2020 census tract lines and extended into water areas. returnCountOnly gives 85 features in total and 53 with WATER=0, so the claim's "about 50 polygons" is correct only after filtering WATER=0. A point query at the Space Needle (inSR=4326) returned GEN_ALIAS "Queen Anne", NEIGHDIST "Magnolia/Queen Anne", DETL_NAMES "Queen Anne, Lower Queen Anne, Uptown, Seattle Center, Westlake", so name/alias/district fields work as claimed. Item licenseInfo reads "PDDL | This item is meant for public access and use. The City of Seattle makes no representation or warranty as to its accuracy ... We do reserve the right to alter, suspend, re-host, or retire this service at any time and without notice"; accessInformation is "City of Seattle, Office of Planning and Community Development". PDDL is fully compatible with a public hobby site; build-time baking is sensible given the retire-at-any-time language. The companion "Community Reporting Areas (2020) - Redistricting Data 1990-2020" exists as item baf97a0c4cda4242a3a0a14470e47621 (slug SeattleCityGIS::community-reporting-areas-2020-redistricting-data-1990-2020), also PDDL-1.0, backed by CRA_90_20_PL/FeatureServer/0 with 53 records and fields F1990_/F2000_/F2010_/F2020_PL_data_TOT_POP plus race/ethnicity, under/over 18, housing units and group-quarters counts; a live sample returned Arbor Heights 6,247 (1990) -> 6,353 (2020). Its key fields are NEIGH_NO, NEIGH_NAME, NEIGHDIST_NO, NEIGHDIST_NAME rather than CRA_NO/GEN_ALIAS/NEIGHDIST, so the join is NEIGH_NO = CRA_NO. The FGDC metadata (a public copy in github.com/tannewt/seattle-redistricting) states the CRA geography was "adopted as a standard, consistent, citywide community-oriented geography for reporting purposes across all departments" and "is not an attempt to identify neighborhood boundaries as defined by neighborhoods themselves", which supports the claim's quoted 'official' with that caveat; the Neighborhood Map Atlas is labelled unofficial by the City. No API key was needed for any request. Caveats, none of which refute the claim: native spatial reference is EPSG:2926 (WA State Plane North, feet), so request outSR=4326 or f=geojson; exclude the blob field SE_ANNO_CAD_DATA from outFields; maxRecordCount is 2000 (fine for 85 features). Web search budget ran out partway through, but the primary endpoints were reachable, so the findings rest on direct observation rather than search snippets.

gaps:
1. No dated historic-shoreline or regrade polygon layer exists on any Seattle/King County portal; the Burke Waterlines GIS was never published. The only vector sources for the 1850s saltwater shoreline are the UW River History Project T-sheet geodatabase and NOAA's data-rescue shorelines (both need a one-time manual download, and the UW site is aging). Pre-1916 Lake Washington / Lake Union shorelines and the Black River exist only on the USGS 1894/1897 topo sheets (raster) and in a 1981 USGS report; the lake dropped 8-12 ft depending on source (HistoryLink 9 ft, Wikipedia 8.8 ft). Regrade extents must be hand-drawn from HistoryLink/Wikipedia descriptions or taken from the undated Modified Land 'graded' polygons.
2. Plat recording dates: no dataset. King County extracts give PlatName/Lot/Block but the year platted lives only in Recorder 'Landmark' and the WA Digital Archives index (manual lookup, no API).
3. Streetcar lines by year: no GIS anywhere (american-rail-history has no Seattle file). OHM's 759 dated railway ways are the only geodata; a full by-year network requires hand-tracing the 1920/1933 city track maps.
4. Seattle Historical Sites (5,000+ properties with year built/architect) has no export or API; the only citywide year-built source stays the Assessor/PARCEL_GEO. The Landmarks layer has no year-built field (join needed).
5. Community Reporting Areas: FeatureServer path and field names unverified (Hub item confirmed). City Clerk Neighborhoods service is retired.
6. Photos: Flickr API keys are now Pro-only and the endpoint lacks dependable CORS, so the SMA Flickr stream must be reached through its Wikimedia Commons mirror (rate-limited, mostly ungeocoded, so neighborhood assignment is by caption text). SMA Digital Collections has no API and discourages scraping. SPL CONTENTdm CORS unverified. MOHAI requires permission beyond fair use; Paul Dorpat columns are link-out only. Sophie Frye Bass's 'Pig-Tail Days' (1937) has no online scan and its renewal status was not resolved, so treat as copyrighted.
7. Other counties: only Snohomish's year-built file is confirmed by the county's own description; Pierce (Improvement/Built-As), Spokane (Property Info), Clark (building table), Kitsap (Dwellings.txt), Thurston and Whatcom need one manual read of their data dictionaries. The statewide geo.wa.gov parcel layer has no year built; the UW statewide parcel DB with YearBuilt is not public.
8. DAHP register layers have conflicting access statements (DAHP: free download; WSDOT: agreement required); NPS NRHP + Wikipedia + Wikidata is the clean fallback.
9. Wikipedia has no 'List of streets in Seattle' and no 'Timeline of Tacoma'; OSM etymology tags in Seattle are sparse, so street-name origins need a curated file.
10. Not verified live this session (sandbox blocked all but S3/GitHub): KingCo_Aerial_1936 tile origin, SPL/OCLC CORS, King County Historic_Landmarks fields, Tacoma/Spokane layer names, HathiTrust full-view status of Meany 1923, figshare license on Ketcherside's CSV.
recommendation:
BUILD-TIME DESIGN (scripts/build-wa.mjs run by a monthly GitHub Actions job, output committed under public/data/, each file with a sources.json entry carrying name, URL, license and fetch date):
- seattle/neighborhoods.topojson (94 Map Atlas polygons + 20 districts, PDDL), seattle/cra.topojson (official reporting areas with 1990-2020 counts), seattle/annexations.topojson + annexations.json (45 polygons, year/ordinance/archive link, the seven annexed towns' dates), seattle/districts.topojson (8 historic districts with designation year), seattle/landmarks.json (517 points deduped by LANDNO, yrBuilt joined from PARCEL_GEO, Wikipedia title), seattle/modified_land.topojson (367 fill/graded polygons hand-tagged with the dated event: tideflat fill 1895-1917, Denny 1898-1930, Jackson 1907-09, Dearborn 1909-12, Harbor Island 1903-09, Duwamish straightening 1913-20, lakebed exposed 1916), seattle/shoreline_1850s.topojson (clipped from the UW T-sheet geodatabase, one-time manual download), seattle/rail.geojson (OHM Overpass extract of railway ways with start/end dates), seattle/street_old_names.json (Ketcherside 1895/1906/1907 tables), seattle/street_origins.json (curated ~120 arterials, own words + source link), seattle/historylink.json (neighborhood -> thumbnail essay), seattle/timeline.json (parsed Wikipedia Timeline of Seattle; same for Spokane), seattle/photos_manifest.json (Commons SMA categories, throttled 1 req/2-3 s, bucketed by neighborhood/street text and decade), seattle/plats.json (hand-curated year platted for the ~150 commonest PlatName values).
- King County: yrbuilt/<major3>.json shards (PIN -> yrBuilt, yrRenovated, plat, lot, block) from the Assessor extracts (33 MB zips, weekly).
- Statewide: incorporations.json (281 cities from the muni-incorporation CSV, cross-checked with MRSC; add Seattle's 1865/1867/1869 and the annexed towns by hand), populations.json (OFM 1890-2020 decennial), gnis_wa.json (populated places, civil units, historical features, with GNIS history text), placename_origins.json (Meany 1923 entries for counties/cities/water bodies, PD), nrhp_wa.json (NPS + Wikipedia + Wikidata), counties/<fips>_yrbuilt shards for Pierce, Snohomish, Spokane, Clark as each data dictionary is confirmed.
- Target: every Seattle-specific file under 300 KB gzipped; shards fetched on demand by county/Major prefix so a phone loads <500 KB per address.
RUNTIME (browser, no keys): Nominatim/Photon geocode; Seattle PARCEL_GEO year built; KC PropertyInfo layer 2 plat name (and geo.wa.gov parcels elsewhere); local point-in-polygon on the baked TopoJSON for neighborhood/CRA/annexation/district/fill; USGS Historical Topo exportImage (1894/1897/1909/1949 sheets) and the King County 1936 aerial tiles as dated map layers; OHM tiles date-filtered; UW CONTENTdm (and SPL if CORS confirms) neighborhood photo search; Commons geosearch; Wikipedia summaries/sections; link-outs to HistoryLink, SMA Digital Collections, Seattle Historical Sites, Landmark plats, MOHAI, Dorpat, Burke Waterlines.
TIME CONTROL BEHAVIOUR FOR THE SEATTLE RINGS: house ring hides before yrBuilt and says 'on fill since c.1895-1917' or 'ground regraded 1907-09' from modified_land tags; block ring names the addition and (where curated) its plat year, links the nearest Sanborn sheet year and shows the 1936 aerial at the 1936 stop; street ring shows the pre-1895 name before Dec 23 1895 (Ord 4044), the pre-1961 directional style before Ord 89910, the nearest dated streetcar/cable line from rail.geojson, and the curated origin sentence; neighborhood ring shows annexation year ('not yet Seattle' before it), GNIS historical names (Latona, Ross, Edgewater, Hillman City), the HistoryLink thumbnail link and photos from the manifest for the chosen decade; city ring shows population for the decade and events from timeline.json.
DATED FACTS TO ENCODE (source in brackets): Sept 1851 Collins party settles on the Duwamish (Wikipedia Timeline of Seattle); Nov 13 1851 Denny Party lands at Alki (HL 5392); Apr 1852 move to Elliott Bay, May 23 1853 first plats filed (HL 303); Jan 26 1856 Battle of Seattle (HL 5208); 1865 incorporated, 1867 disincorporated, Dec 2 1869 reincorporated (HL 303); Sept 23 1884 horse streetcars (HL 2690); Sept 28 1887 Yesler Way cable cars (HL 2707); Mar 31 1889 first electric streetcar (HL 2691); Jun 6 1889 Great Fire, 64 acres (HL 21090); Nov 11 1889 statehood; 1891 north annexation to 85th St (Annexation layer); Jul 29 1895 tideflat filling begins, ~92% filled by 1917 (HL 2986, 22852); Dec 1895 citywide street renaming Ord 4044 (Ketcherside); Jul 17 1897 Portland arrives with Klondike gold (HL 687); 1898-Jan 6 1899 Denny Regrade phase 1, 1903-Oct 31 1911 phase 2, 1928-Dec 10 1930 phase 3 (HL 708-711, 21204); Sept 25 1902 Seattle-Tacoma Interurban (HL 2669); Oct 20 1905 South Seattle annexed; Jan 7/Jan 15/May 3/May 29/Jul 24/Sept 12 1907 Southeast Seattle, Ravenna, Columbia and South Park, Ballard, West Seattle, Rainier Beach annexed (SMA reference); May 27 1907-Dec 1909 Jackson Street Regrade (HL 23118); Jun 1-Oct 16 1909 AYP Exposition (HL 8892); Aug 31 1909-autumn 1912 Dearborn Regrade (HL 23149); 1909/early 1910 Harbor Island completed (HL 3631); Apr 11 1910 Georgetown annexed; Apr 30 1910 Seattle-Everett Interurban (HL 5341); Oct 14 1913 Duwamish straightening begins, done ~1920 (HL 2986, 21333); 1916 Montlake Cut opens, Aug 28 1916 Lake Washington lowering begins (~9 ft), Black River dries (HL 1444); Jul 4 1917 Ballard Locks dedicated; 1919 city buys the streetcar system (HL 2707); 1936 aerial survey and peak 26-28 streetcar lines; Aug 10 1940 last Yesler cable car, April 1941 last streetcar (Seattle Times/HL); 1945 Wedgwood annexed (Ord 73879); 1953-54 north annexations to 145th St (Lake City); 1961 directional designations Ord 89910 (SMA); 1970-2011 historic districts designated; 1982-2005 Waterfront Streetcar; 2007 and 2016 modern streetcars.
PRIORITY ORDER: (1) bake Map Atlas, annexations, landmarks+yrBuilt, modified land, timeline, incorporations, populations, GNIS (all verified or near-verified, all free); (2) Commons SMA photo manifest and UW CONTENTdm runtime search; (3) 1850s shoreline from UW T-sheets and the USGS 1894 sheet as the dated map stop; (4) street old names + curated origins; (5) OHM rail extract; (6) other-county year-built shards starting with Snohomish and Pierce; (7) optional hand-traced streetcar network and Allmaps Sanborn overlays. Keep 'thin ring' honesty everywhere: say 'no record' rather than guess a plat year or a streetcar line.

Long, The Newberry Library'. 7) The Comprehensive Database columns are FIPS, STATE, NAME, ID, VERSION, START_DATE, END_DATE, CREATION_OR_CHANGE, CITATION, START_N, END_N, DATASET; its START_DATE/END_DATE are text like '22 12 1845 0:00:00' (dd mm yyyy), so parse START_N/END_N (yyyymmdd) instead. 8) The online US_HistCounties_Metadata2.htm and WA_Metadata2.htm URLs are intermittently behind a BitNinja anti-bot CAPTCHA (HTTP 403) and one fetch was reset; fetch the zip, which contains WA_Metadata2.htm, rather than relying on those pages. 9) The 'WA county lines have not changed since 2000' note could not be verified here (no search budget); treat as unverified. 10) ogr2ogr is not guaranteed on the build machine; the GitHub Actions runner can apt-install gdal-bin, or the npm 'shapefile' package can do the conversion in Node without GDAL.

sources.name: Newberry U.S. Historical States and Territories (edition 2.0, 2011)
sources.what_it_gives: Polygons for every configuration of US states and territories, dated to the day, 3 Sep 1783 - 31 Dec 2000, derived from the county dataset. sources.license_terms: Same ambiguous Newberry terms as the county atlas (reuse for any lawful purpose per download page; CC BY-NC-SA deed in zip; attribution required in any reading).
sources.example_request: Download the 0.01-degree generalized zip (~2 MB); filter polygons whose geometry intersects today's WA outline; keep NAME, START_DATE, END_DATE, CHANGE; emit data/state/territory_versions.json (about 8 polygons).
sources.size_or_volume: ~2 MB generalized zip; a handful of polygons relevant to WA.

verdict.reasoning:
Newberry's own hosts (publications.newberry.org, www.newberry.org), Wikipedia and HistoryLink are egress-blocked here and the web-search budget was exhausted, so I verified against the Newberry site's source repository on GitHub (NewberryDIS/ahcb, contact dis@newberry.org; fetched via raw.githubusercontent.com and GitHub code search) plus a third-party CSV dump of the shapefile's attribute table (localgeohistoryproject/county-boundaries-topology, 220 state/territory versions, derived from US_HistStateTerr.shp).

CONFIRMED: (1) downloads/united_states.html exists in the site source with a "US Historical States & Territories (1783-2000)" table listing Full 110 MB, Gen0001 53 MB, Gen001 14 MB, Gen01 2 MB, Gen05 .6 MB (GIS zips) plus KMZ variants - exactly the claimed sizes/tolerances. (2) documents/US_HistStateTerr_Metadata2.htm: title "U.S. Historical States and Territories", Edition 2.0, publication date 20111001, time period 17830903-20001231, "All changes are dated to the day", "generated from the U.S. Historical Counties dataset", attribute fields NAME, ID, VERSION, START_DATE, END_DATE, CHANGE, CITATION, START_N, END_N, AREA_SQMI, TERR_TYPE, FULL_NAME, ABBR_NAME, NAME_START; WGS84 unprojected shapefile. (3) License wording is as the claim describes: download page says data may be "reused for any lawful purpose, commercial or non-commercial, without licensing or permission fees to the library. Please note that some of these files contain the original, out-of-date copyright license; these can be ignored", while the sidebar says each zip contains a "Copy of the free access Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike Creative Commons License" and the metadata docs say "Free for use under an Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike Creative Commons License"; footer defers to newberry.org/rights-and-reproductions (unreadable from here). Metadata1 gives a Preferred Style for Citation (Siczewicz, Peter. U.S. Historical States and Territories. Emily Kelley, digital comp. Dataset. Atlas of Historical County Boundaries, ed. John H. Long. Chicago: The Newberry Library, 2011). Either reading is compatible with a non-commercial hobby site that attributes; under the CC BY-NC-SA reading the derived territory_versions.json should itself be CC BY-NC-SA. (4) Washington dates match the Newberry WA_Consolidated_Chronology and the attribute table: Oregon Territory 1848-08-14; Washington Territory 1853-03-02 "included all of present Washington and parts of present Idaho and Montana"; enlarged 1859-02-14; Idaho Territory 1863-03-03 (Newberry cites U.S. Stat. vol. 12 ch. 117; the Wikipedia "4 Mar" aside could not be checked); statehood 1889-11-11. (5) Build-time use is appropriate (zipped shapefiles); a third-party package (ropensci/USAboundariesData) records fetching from this URL on 2025-10-08, so the host was live a year ago, though I could not confirm reachability today.

CORRECTIONS (details wrong, not the source): (a) 21 Oct 1872 San Juan Islands is NOT a version boundary in the state/territory shapefile - Washington Territory v4 runs 1863-03-03 to 1889-11-10 unbroken, no "Uncertain Boundary Area" polygon exists for the islands (the only UBA row is Lake of the Woods-Rockies 1804-1818), and the chronology entry is explicitly marked "[no change]". The date is only available as text in the WA county chronology document. (b) "Oregon Country (unorganized)" is coded TERR_TYPE "Other" and spans 1804-10-01 to 1846-06-14 only; a separate "Oregon Unorg. FT" (TERR_TYPE Unorganized Territory) covers 1846-06-15 to 1848-08-13. No polygon covers present WA before 1 Oct 1804 even though the dataset starts in 1783. (c) There is an extra WA Territory version the claim omits: v3 1861-03-02 to 1863-03-02 (Nebraska Territory gained part of Shoshone). (d) "About 8 polygons" is right for polygons that actually cover WA ground (Oregon Country, Oregon Unorg. FT, Oregon Terr v1, WA Terr v1-v4, WA state), but a plain "intersects today's WA outline" filter will also pick up neighbours sharing a boundary (Oregon Terr v2, Oregon state, Idaho Territory v1-3, Idaho, Montana Territory/state); use point-in-polygon or area-overlap instead.
verdict.corrected_facts: 1. San Juan Islands arbitration (21 Oct 1872) does not create a polygon version in US_HistStateTerr; Washington Territory version 4 is 1863-03-03 to 1889-11-10 with no break. The 1872 date appears only in the WA consolidated county chronology, marked "[no change]". 2. Dataset's Washington-area sequence is: Oregon Country (TERR_TYPE Other) 1804-10-01 to 1846-06-14; Oregon Unorg. FT (Unorganized Territory) 1846-06-15 to 1848-08-13; Oregon Territory v1 1848-08-14 to 1853-03-01; Washington Territory v1 1853-03-02 to 1859-02-13, v2 1859-02-14 to 1861-03-01, v3 1861-03-02 to 1863-03-02, v4 1863-03-03 to 1889-11-10; Washington state 1889-11-11 to 2000-12-31. Nothing covers WA before 1804-10-01. 3. Metadata publication date is 1 Oct 2011, Edition 2.0; full zip is 110 MB per the official page (a third-party mirror says 100 MB). 4. sources.name: OpenHistoricalMap - Newberry county import (dated county boundary relations) + WA coverage/licensing summary
sources.what_it_gives: OHM imported the entire Newberry county atlas (import file 4/16 Jan 2023; project page says import complete, post-processing ongoing): boundary=administrative admin_level=6 relations with start_date/end_date (Newberry START_DATE -> start_date) and nl_ahcb:*/newberry-namespaced id tags. sources.coverage: Statewide county boundaries 1845-2000 via the import; city-level detail Seattle only; WA statewide otherwise sparse.
sources.license_terms: OHM database CC0 since 3 Aug 2022 (elements may override with license=* tags; CC BY / CC BY-SA features exist). Tilesets: General and Boundary tiles public domain unless noted; Landmasses tileset derived from OSM coastlines is ODbL. sources.example_request: POST https://overpass-api.openhistoricalmap.org/api/interpreter with: [out:json][timeout:25]; is_in(47.62,-122.35)->.a; rel(pivot.a)[boundary=administrative][admin_level=6]; out tags; -> then filter client-side by start_date <= date < end_date (treat missing end_date as open). sources.notes: Recommendation: use the Newberry shapefile at build time as the source of truth for the county ring (no runtime dependency, no start_date bug) and let OHM tiles simply draw the matching boundary; use Overpass only as an optional enrichment.
