sources.example_request: Strategy: (1) seed data/historylink.json from the Wikidata 'HistoryLink essay number' property (SPARQL above); (2) at build time fetch File/9143 once (plain HTML, Cheerio) and parse every 'Name -- Thumbnail History' into {name, type: county|city|neighborhood, essay}; (3) hand-curate a small overrides file for multi-part essays and 'Seattle Neighborhoods:' prefixes; (4) match to places.json by normalized name + county; (5) in the UI show 'Read the HistoryLink Thumbnail History' per ring. Also harvest 'X incorporates on DATE' essays for incorporation dates.
sources.size_or_volume: Index page ~400 links; final table a few hundred rows.
sources.notes: HistoryLink's search endpoint (/Search/Results?TopicId=11 etc.) is HTML only and fragile; the Index page is the stable entry point. Dated event essays ('This Week Then') could later feed the year-by-year timeline for city rings, but only as titles + links.

sources.name: WA DNR Washington Geological Survey - 100K_Surface_Geology_WA_GeMS (layer 11 map units + table 13 DMU)
sources.what_it_gives: Statewide 1:100,000 surface geology polygons. Layer 11 fields: MAP_UNIT_100K, MAP_UNIT_100K_ID_CONFIDENCE, MAP_UNIT_100K_LABEL, MAP_UNIT_100K_SYMBOL (short unit symbol e.g. Qgt, Qfg, Mvb), MAP_UNIT_100K_NOTES, MAP_UNIT_ORIGINAL, MAP_UNIT_100K_ID, MAP_UNIT_100K_QUAD_NAME, MAP_UNIT_100K_QUAD_UNIT, GLOBALID (no age/description). Table 13 (Description of Map Units; JSON/PBF only): DMU_100K_MAP_UNIT, DMU_100K_FULL_NAME (e.g. 'Pleistocene continental glacial till'), DMU_100K_AGE, DMU_100K_DESCRIPTION, DMU_100K_QUAD_NAME, DMU_FEATURE_QUAD_UNIT, DMU_100K_ID; join layer11.MAP_UNIT_100K_QUAD_UNIT = table13.DMU_FEATURE_QUAD_UNIT (1:1). Other layers: 0 Vents, 1 Orientation, 2 Geochron, 3 Generic Points, 4 Fossil, 5 Lines, 6 Folds, 7 Faults, 8 Dikes, 9 Contacts, 10 Overlays, 12 Data Sources. Lithology is embedded in the description text (no separate lithology column). ArcGIS 11.5, maxRecordCount 2000, JSON/geoJSON/PBF.
sources.coverage: Entire state (Space Needle -> Qgt Vashon till; Spokane -> Qfg Missoula outburst-flood deposits; Rainier summit -> ice). Also site3: 24K/25-99K surface geology, landslides, tsunami.
sources.license_terms: WGS 'Disclaimers and Citation Guidelines': all materials 'free for you to use in any way you choose', commercial or not, with credit; each geodatabase is an official WGS publication with a suggested citation in its metadata; the AGOL Hub listing says 'No License Provided' (contradiction; the WGS page governs). Data 'as is', screening tool only.
sources.example_request: GET https://gis.dnr.wa.gov/site1/rest/services/Public_Geology/100K_Surface_Geology_WA_GeMS/MapServer/11/query?geometry=-122.349,47.620&geometryType=esriGeometryPoint&inSR=4326&spatialRel=esriSpatialRelIntersects&outFields=MAP_UNIT_100K_SYMBOL,MAP_UNIT_100K_LABEL,MAP_UNIT_100K_QUAD_UNIT&returnGeometry=false&f=json  then  .../MapServer/13/query?where=DMU_FEATURE_QUAD_UNIT='<value>'&outFields=DMU_100K_FULL_NAME,DMU_100K_AGE,DMU_100K_DESCRIPTION&f=json
sources.size_or_volume: Thousands of polygons statewide; two small point queries per visit.
sources.notes: Build-time option: download the DMU table once (table 13, paged 2000/req) into data/geology/dmu.json so the runtime needs only the layer-11 point query. The unit symbols also give the ice-age ring for free: Qg* = glaciated (Vashon/Fraser), Qfg/Qf* = Missoula-flood deposits, Qa = Holocene alluvium, Qls = landslide, Mvb/Mv(...) = Columbia River Basalt (17-6 Ma), Ev* = Eocene Siletzia/Crescent basalt, etc. File geodatabase downloads exist for the whole dataset if a pre-baked statewide simplification is wanted.

sources.name: WA DNR Geochronology, Volcanic_Vents, Earthquakes_and_Faults MapServers
sources.what_it_gives: Geochronology/MapServer: 0 Argon, 1 Uranium, 2 Radiocarbon, 3 Fission Track, 4 Fossils, 5 Luminescence, 6 Other. Layer 0 fields: AGE_MA, ERROR_MA, AGE_MODIFIER, ANALYSIS_TYPE, MATERIAL_DATED, GEOLOGIC_UNIT_NAME, LABEL_TXT, SYMBOLOGY (period), LATITUDE, LONGITUDE, COUNTY_NAME; layer 2 (radiocarbon): CONVENTIONAL_AGE_BP, MEASURED_AGE_BP, TWO_SIGMA_CAL_AGE_DATA, LABEL_TXT. Volcanic_Vents/MapServer: layer 0 Vent Locations (vent name, type, age fields not captured by the probe; read /0?f=pjson). Earthquakes_and_Faults/MapServer: 0 Fault Trenches, 1 Historical Earthquake Damage, 2 Quaternary Active Folds, 4 Relocated Earthquakes >1M, 5 Earthquakes >1M, 12 Quaternary Active Faults; tables 6 Historical Earthquake Photos, 8 Fault Citations.
sources.coverage: Statewide dated samples (e.g. 14.7 +/- 1.8 Ma K-Ar tuff at 47.5758/-122.1132), all Cascade and minor vents, historical quakes (1872 North Cascades, 1949/1965/2001 Puget Sound) and active faults (Seattle, Tacoma, SWIF, etc.).
sources.license_terms: Same WGS free-with-credit terms as above.
sources.example_request: GET https://gis.dnr.wa.gov/site1/rest/services/Public_Geology/Geochronology/MapServer/0/query?geometry=-122.5,47.4,-122.1,47.8&geometryType=esriGeometryEnvelope&inSR=4326&outFields=AGE_MA,ERROR_MA,MATERIAL_DATED,GEOLOGIC_UNIT_NAME,LABEL_TXT&returnGeometry=true&outSR=4326&f=geojson
sources.size_or_volume: Thousands of points statewide; pre-bake per-county summaries at build time (nearest N dated samples, nearest vent, faults within 25 km).
sources.notes: For the 'millions of years' slider: nearest dated sample + its unit gives a sentence like 'Rock 3 km from here was dated 14.7 Ma'. Pair with Macrostrat (already verified) for the regional column and GPlates for plate position.

sources.name: WA DNR Public_Boundaries/WADNR_PUBLIC_Cadastre_OpenData (PLSS sections, townships, county boundaries) - site3
sources.what_it_gives: Layer 7 Public Land Survey Sections, Public Land Survey Townships, Layer 2 WA Legal Descriptions, Layer 11 County Boundaries (current), State Outline/Boundary, DNR units. Gives the township/range/section for a point (Willamette Meridian), i.e. the 1850s-1880s 'section' ring and the key for linking to GLO original survey plats/land patents and to Donation Land Claims. A sibling service Public_Boundaries/WADNR_PUBLIC_Public_Land_Survey also exists; WA DOR has Base/WADOR_Base_PLSS at webgis.dor.wa.gov.
sources.coverage: Statewide.
sources.license_terms: DNR open data ('Open Access to DNR data'); credit WA DNR.
sources.example_request: GET .../MapServer/7/query?geometry=-122.349,47.620&geometryType=esriGeometryPoint&inSR=4326&outFields=*&returnGeometry=false&f=json  (gis.dnr.wa.gov echoes Origin per the probe, so this works in the browser; confirm field names from /7?f=pjson).
sources.size_or_volume: ~60k sections statewide; point query only.
sources.notes: Then link out to BLM GLO Records (https://glorecords.blm.gov/ -> Search Documents -> Patents -> State WA, Meridian Willamette, T/R/S) for the first federal patentee and date; GLO has no API and its bulk CSVs were withdrawn in 2022, so this stays a link-out.

sources.name: DAHP WISAARD - Historic Property Inventory and State/National Register properties & districts (FeatureServer)
sources.what_it_gives: Statewide inventory of surveyed historic buildings/structures (points layer 0 HistoricPropertyInventory_pnts, lines layer 1 HPI_Lines) with (2017 metadata) Historic_ID, ResourceID, Loc_FullAddress, SiteNameHistoric, TaxParcel_No, FieldSiteNo and typically build year/style/architect in the inventory form; sibling services DAHP_Register_Properties and DAHP_Register_Districts (Washington Heritage Register + NRHP listings with listing dates). Mirrored on geo.wa.gov as downloadable layers; updated quarterly; last data update 3 Sep 2025. Archaeological sites are withheld; historic buildings are public without login.
sources.coverage: Statewide; DAHP says >600,000 historic sites recorded (inventory points are a subset); Seattle's 517 City Landmarks are a separate city layer (probe).
sources.license_terms: Hub lists the inventory under a 'custom license' and the register layers as no rights restrictions / public; data 'AS IS'. Credit 'Washington State Department of Archaeology & Historic Preservation (DAHP)'. Verify the custom-license text before bulk redistribution; a point-query at runtime plus link-out is safe.
sources.example_request: GET https://wisaard.dahp.wa.gov/server/rest/services/Hosted/DAHP_Historic_Property_Inventory/FeatureServer/0/query?geometry=-122.35,47.60,-122.32,47.63&geometryType=esriGeometryEnvelope&inSR=4326&outFields=*&resultRecordCount=50&f=geojson (MaxRecordCount 2000; confirm CORS by reading the response headers once from the browser; otherwise harvest at build time by county).
sources.size_or_volume: Inventory download ~34 MB; register properties a few thousand points.
sources.notes: This is the statewide 'is there a known historic building on/near this lot' layer and the best non-King source of build years for notable buildings. WISAARD's public map (https://dahp.wa.gov/find-a-historic-place) is the link-out.

sources.name: NPS National Register of Historic Places - spatial locations (MapServer + public file geodatabase)
sources.what_it_gives: Points (and some polygons) for all unrestricted NRHP listings with NRIS reference number, name, listing date, resource type; bulk NRIS_CR_Standards_Public.gdb.zip with the full NRIS attribute tables; ArcGIS Online copy on public-nps.opendata.arcgis.com.
sources.coverage: Nationwide; ~1,500-1,700 WA listings (count not verified). Metadata updated 2 Apr 2026.
sources.license_terms: US Government work, public domain ('for general public distribution'); restricted/sensitive sites excluded.
sources.example_request: Build: query .../nrhp_locations/MapServer/0/query?where=STATE='WA'&outFields=*&f=geojson (page with resultOffset) or ogr2ogr the gdb; emit data/nrhp_wa.geojson (~300 KB).
sources.size_or_volume: ~1.6k WA points.
sources.notes: Overlaps DAHP's register layer; keep NPS as the public-domain fallback and for listing dates/ref numbers (link to https://npgallery.nps.gov/NRHP/AssetDetail?assetID=... or the NRHP PDF nomination, which often has a full building history).

sources.name: USFS Tribal Lands Ceded to the United States (Royce 'Indian Land Cessions in the United States', 1899) - EDW_TribalCessionLands_01
sources.what_it_gives: Polygons of every treaty/statute land cession (CESSNUM = Royce map cession number) with a companion table (layer 2 / S_USA.TribalCededLandsTable) linking to treaty name, date, tribes, statute/executive order text. For WA this encodes the 1854-55 Stevens treaties (Medicine Creek 26 Dec 1854, Point Elliott 22 Jan 1855, Point No Point 26 Jan 1855, Neah Bay 31 Jan 1855, Walla Walla/Yakama/Nez Perce June 1855, Quinault 1855-56) and later cessions, i.e. 'which treaty covered this spot and when'. Layer 1 polygons: JSON/GeoJSON/PBF, max 2000; Hub/data.gov offer CSV/GeoJSON/KML/shapefile downloads.
sources.coverage: Whole US; 752 polygons / 1,172 table entries; last updated Aug 2022.
sources.license_terms: US Government work (USDA Forest Service), public domain; cite 'USDA Forest Service, Tribal Lands Ceded to the United States (Royce)'.
sources.example_request: Build: .../MapServer/1/query?geometry=-124.9,45.5,-116.9,49.1&geometryType=esriGeometryEnvelope&inSR=4326&outFields=*&f=geojson then join layer 2 on CESSNUM; simplify; emit data/cessions_wa.geojson (~20 polygons).
sources.size_or_volume: WA subset a few hundred KB after simplification.
sources.notes: Gives the 1855 'treaty' event for the county/region rings and the pre-treaty 'ceded by' tribe names. Present carefully with the standard caveat that cession maps record the US government's view; pair with Native Land Digital for present-day nations' own territory claims.

sources.name: Native Land Digital API (territories, languages, treaties polygons)
sources.what_it_gives: GeoJSON polygons of Indigenous territories, languages and treaties with names, colors and links to each nation's page; full-dataset endpoints /api/polygons/geojson/{territories|languages|treaties}?key=...; point query endpoints. For the Seattle area returns e.g. Duwamish, Suquamish, Coast Salish, Muckleshoot, Snoqualmie; statewide ~40-60 polygons.
sources.coverage: Worldwide; good WA coverage (Coast Salish, Sahaptin, Interior Salish, Chinookan nations).
sources.license_terms: API key required since late 2024 (free signup, accept API terms). Data Sovereignty Treaty: credit Native Land Digital, acknowledge Indigenous communities as custodians, do not monetize/alter/misuse; boundaries are not official or legal; add their disclaimer. External listings disagree on the CC license (CC BY vs CC BY-NC-SA 1.0 vs 'custom'); treat as custom non-commercial + attribution.
sources.example_request: Build (key in a GitHub Actions secret, never in the browser): curl 'https://native-land.ca/api/polygons/geojson/territories?key=$NLD_KEY' | clip to WA bbox | simplify -> data/native_land_wa.geojson; re-fetch monthly; render with their disclaimer text.
sources.size_or_volume: Full territories file ~20-30 MB; WA clip < 1 MB.
sources.notes: Because the terms discourage altering the data, keep polygons unmodified except clipping/simplifying for display and say so in the credit line.

sources.name: EPA Level III / IV Ecoregions MapServer (region-of-the-state ring)
sources.what_it_gives: Layer 11 Level III polygons (US_L3NAME), layer 7 Level IV polygons (US_L4NAME), labels layer 5; Dec 2011 vintage; also on geodata.epa.gov and as an Esri feature layer (updated Mar 2026). WA's nine Level III ecoregions: Coast Range, Puget Lowland, North Cascades, Cascades, Eastern Cascades Slopes and Foothills, Columbia Plateau, Blue Mountains, Northern Rockies, Willamette Valley (Clark County only). Alternative 'region' framings: WA DNR's nine geologic provinces (Okanogan Highlands, North Cascades, South Cascades, Olympic Mountains, Willapa Hills, Puget Lowland, Columbia Basin, Blue Mountains, Portland Basin) on dnr.wa.gov (text/maps only; no GIS layer found).
sources.coverage: Nationwide; WA fully covered.
sources.license_terms: EPA metadata: open for public access and use, no restrictions (US Government work). Credit 'U.S. EPA Ecoregions (Omernik)'.
sources.example_request: Build: .../MapServer/11/query?geometry=-124.9,45.5,-116.9,49.1&geometryType=esriGeometryEnvelope&inSR=4326&outFields=US_L3CODE,US_L3NAME&f=geojson -> clip to WA -> simplify 0.005 deg -> data/regions_wa.geojson (~9 polygons, <200 KB).
sources.size_or_volume: 9 Level III polygons for WA (Level IV ~60).
sources.notes: Recommend a hand-written data/regions.json that maps each ecoregion (or county) to a human 'region of the state' name (Puget Sound, Olympic Peninsula, Southwest Washington, Columbia Basin, Palouse, Okanogan Highlands, Yakima Valley, Spokane/Inland Northwest) with a short deep-time blurb (Siletzia, Columbia River Basalts, Missoula floods, Cordilleran ice), since no official 'regions of Washington' layer exists.

sources.name: USGS Historical Topographic Map Collection (HTMC) index + GeoTIFF/GeoPDF downloads, via OpenGeoMetadata gov.usgs.htmc (CC0 metadata) and prd-tnm S3
sources.what_it_gives: Verified by download of the WA index maps (index-maps/htmc/usgs-htmc-index-wa-{scale}.geojson): per-sheet footprint polygons with label, title, datePub, dateSurvey/dateReprnt, scale, recId (USGS scan id), websiteUrl (ScienceBase), download (GeoTIFF on https://prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com/StagedProducts/Maps/HistoricalTopo/GeoTIFF/WA/...), thumbUrl (JPEG). WA counts/years: 1:125,000 247 sheets 1895-1942 (117 printed in the 1900s; Seattle 1897 surveyed 1895, imprints 1901/1904/1906/1909); 1:62,500 828 sheets 1894-1973 (438 in the 1950s); 1:24,000 3,381 sheets 1948-2005; 1:100,000 56 (1975-1993); 1:250,000 76 (1909-1965); 1:48,000 6 (1912-1939). Repository rebuilds daily from USGS's nightly inventory (historicaltopo.zip).
sources.coverage: Statewide WA, 1894-2005 (earliest quads: Seattle/Tacoma/Snohomish/Mt Rainier area 1894-1897; most of eastern WA first mapped 1900s-1910s at 1:125,000).
sources.license_terms: Maps: US public domain (USGS). Metadata records: CC0 1.0. USGS asks for the credit 'Map services and data available from U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program'.
sources.example_request: Build: fetch the six WA index geojsons (~3.3 MB total), drop geometry precision to 4 dp, emit data/topo/wa_index.json [{id, title, scale, year, survey, imprint, bbox, tif, thumb}] (~600 KB; 4,594 sheets). Runtime: point-in-bbox lookup gives 'maps covering this spot, oldest first' with the thumbnail and a link to topoView (https://ngmdb.usgs.gov/topoview/viewer/#...).
sources.size_or_volume: 4,594 WA sheets; index ~3.3 MB raw -> ~0.6 MB compact.
sources.notes: For a public-domain, Esri-free rendered historical map layer: at build time download a curated set of GeoTIFFs (e.g. Seattle 1897 and 1909 1:62,500, Tacoma 1900, Spokane 1901, Olympia 1906...), gdalwarp to EPSG:3857, and tile to PMTiles (z8-14, ~2-8 MB each) committed to the repo or a Pages assets folder; MapLibre reads PMTiles with the pmtiles protocol, no server needed. Keep the Esri ImageServer (below) for everything else.

sources.name: Esri ArcGIS Living Atlas - USGS Historical Topographic Maps ImageServer (historical1.arcgis.com)
sources.what_it_gives: Mosaic of ~181,000 HTMC scans (1:10,000-1:250,000, 1879/1882-2006) with catalog fields Map_Name, Map_Scale, Date_On_Map, Imprint_Year, Year, Download_GeoPDF, View_Thumbnail_Image, Citation, OBJECTID; exportImage of a single sheet via mosaicRule esriMosaicLockRaster (probe verified; CORS echoes origin; Web Mercator). Esri's Topo Explorer app sits on it.
sources.coverage: All of WA, same sheets as HTMC (minus orthophotoquads).
sources.license_terms: Underlying maps public domain (USGS); the hosted service item says 'licensed under the Esri Master License Agreement' and lists access via org/developer accounts, though the probe showed anonymous exportImage works today. Required credit: 'Source: Historical Topographic Map Collection courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey, Esri'. Risk: Esri could require a token later; keep the PMTiles fallback above.
sources.example_request: GET https://historical1.arcgis.com/arcgis/rest/services/USGS_Historical_Topographic_Maps/ImageServer/exportImage?bbox=-13627000,6033000,-13613000,6047000&bboxSR=3857&imageSR=3857&size=1024,1024&format=jpg&mosaicRule={"mosaicMethod":"esriMosaicLockRaster","lockRasterIds":[<OBJECTID>]}&f=image  (OBJECTID from /ImageServer/query?geometry=<lon,lat>&geometryType=esriGeometryPoint&inSR=4326&outFields=Map_Name,Map_Scale,Date_On_Map,Imprint_Year,OBJECTID&f=json)
sources.size_or_volume: One exportImage per pan/zoom; fine for a few sheets per visit.
sources.notes: Time-slider behaviour: pick the sheet with the largest Date_On_Map <= selected year at the best available scale; show the imprint year caption.

sources.name: Library of Congress Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps - Washington cities (loc.gov JSON API + IIIF)
sources.what_it_gives: Public-domain scans of pre-1964 Sanborn atlases for WA cities with per-sheet IIIF (tile.loc.gov/image-services/iiif/service:gmd:gmd428m:g4284m:...), item JSON (dates, sheet counts, city, county, 'location' facets), thumbnails. Per-city evidence: Seattle 32 items (probe), Tacoma from Sep 1885 (10 sheets) through 1912-Jan 1950 volumes (113-115 sheets), Spokane 1902 vol. 2 (124 sheets), 1910 vols. 1-3 (111-116), Walla Walla 8 items 1884-1905/1955, Walla Walla County 23 items (Waitsburg 7, Prescott 3, Wallula 3, Touchet 2), Lincoln County 42 items; item ids follow sanborn09nnn_mmm with WA cities numbered alphabetically (Seattle 09315, Spokane 09331, Tacoma 09345, Walla Walla 09361, Wallula 09362). The LOC says all public-domain sheets are online except some 1923-1930; WA State Library's microfilm set covers 283 WA cities for the post-1923 era (not online).
sources.coverage: Roughly 100+ WA cities/towns, 1884-1963 (most 1888-1912 plus 1950s republications); exact statewide item count not retrievable from the sandbox (the location:washington facet also matches Washington DC/GA).
sources.license_terms: Pre-1964 Sanborn sheets public domain (LOC 'no known restrictions'); credit 'Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division'. LOC rate limits ~20 req/10 s collections, 40/10 s items; no key.
sources.example_request: Build: page https://www.loc.gov/collections/sanborn-maps/?fa=location:washington&fo=json&c=100&sp=N, keep items whose item.location includes a WA county name or whose id matches /^sanborn09[23]\d\d/ (verify range), emit data/sanborn_wa.json [{id, city, county, dates, sheets, thumb, iiif_base}]; runtime: show the nearest city's volumes for the selected year and open the IIIF viewer / LOC page.
sources.size_or_volume: A few hundred items statewide; index JSON < 200 KB.
sources.notes: Sanborn sheets are not georeferenced at LOC; for Seattle a build-time georeference of the 1893/1904/1917 downtown index sheets (QGIS) into PMTiles would be a signature feature; statewide, link-out by city is enough.

sources.name: Library of Congress Chronicling America (loc.gov JSON API) - Washington newspapers 1852-1963
sources.what_it_gives: Full-text-searchable newspaper pages with OCR, dates, titles, city; new site since 4 Aug 2025 (legacy chroniclingamerica.loc.gov API deprecated; use loc.gov API with dl=page, start_date/end_date, location_state, fa=... filters). WA titles contributed by the Washington State Library (115+ titles, ~400k pages 1852-1963), earliest The Columbian (Olympia, 1852-53). Title list: https://www.loc.gov/collections/chronicling-america/titles/?fa=location_state:washington
sources.coverage: Statewide, strongest 1880s-1922; through 1963.
sources.license_terms: Public domain (pre-1930 pages) / LOC 'no known restrictions' on NDNP content; no key; rate-limit politely.
sources.example_request: GET https://www.loc.gov/collections/chronicling-america/?dl=page&fa=location_state:washington&q="Ballard"&start_date=1890-01-01&end_date=1890-12-31&fo=json&c=10  (CORS: www.loc.gov returned ACAO * in the probe; confirm for this collection path once in-browser).
sources.size_or_volume: Hundreds of thousands of WA pages; use only targeted queries (place name + year) with debounce.
sources.notes: Gives the 'what the local paper said that year' panel for the city ring. Washington Digital Newspapers (Veridian, 1.07M pages, no API found) is the link-out for titles/years not in Chronicling America: https://washingtondigitalnewspapers.org/?a=q&txq=<term>&dafyq=<year>&datyq=<year>.

sources.name: Washington State Archives - Digital Archives (digitalarchives.wa.gov)
sources.what_it_gives: No public API (none documented; 2000s-era SOAP plans only). ~267M records (92M online): territorial and state censuses (name-indexed, not tabulations), marriage/naturalization/land records, General Map Collection (1,807 maps 1851-2005: GLO survey sheets, railroad/highway, county and city maps), ~3,000 state photographs, and county assessor series such as 'Thurston County Assessor Real Property Assessment Cards and Photographs 1936-1997' (parcel-number searchable; photos 1936-1971; only partly online). Public web search: People Search, Keyword Search, Detailed Search per series; results capped at 5,000.
sources.coverage: Statewide; depth varies by county/series.
sources.license_terms: State public records; most pre-1964 state photos public domain; per-series rights statements. Link out; do not scrape.
sources.example_request: Link-out URL patterns: https://digitalarchives.wa.gov/Collections/TitleInfo/2303 (Thurston assessor cards; search by parcel number), https://digitalarchives.wa.gov/Collections/TitleInfo/873 (General Map Collection). Build a small data/archives_links.json keyed by county -> relevant series ids.
sources.size_or_volume: n/a (link-out).
sources.notes: Ask the Archives (ajansen@secstate.wa.gov is the historic contact; use the current support site) whether a bulk export of the map collection metadata exists; until then it is a 'go deeper here' link under the county and house rings. The King County assessor property-record cards (1937-72 photos) are at the Puget Sound Regional Branch and are NOT online.

sources.name: Washington State Historical Society - Collections Search (washingtonhistory.org)
sources.what_it_gives: Online catalog of >600,000 photographs (incl. the Asahel Curtis archive, 42,000-60,000 images, digitization ongoing), 90,000 artifacts, 50,000 ephemera; search syntax (+ for AND, quotes for phrase, catalog numbers like 1984.3.22), filter 'has image'. No API; image orders via Image Services; rights per item (WSHS licenses reproductions). Columbia magazine articles separately.
sources.coverage: Statewide, strongest Pierce County/Tacoma and early 20th-century Puget Sound (Curtis).
sources.license_terms: Catalog viewing free; reuse of images requires WSHS permission/fees except where items are public domain; link out only.
sources.example_request: Link-out: https://www.washingtonhistory.org/research/collections-search/?search="<city or neighborhood>" (verify the query parameter in a browser once; the site is a WordPress front end over the collections database).
sources.size_or_volume: n/a (link-out).
sources.notes: Treat like HistoryLink: a curated 'Explore photos at WSHS' link per city; prefer Commons (Seattle Municipal Archives CC BY), LOC (PD), Washington Rural Heritage and library CONTENTdm sites for in-page thumbnails.

sources.name: Washington Rural Heritage (Washington State Library, CONTENTdm) - statewide local-history photos and documents
sources.what_it_gives: CONTENTdm instance aggregating 25+ community collections (public/tribal/academic libraries, museums, private collections) of rural WA: photos, maps, documents with Dublin Core metadata (date, place, rights per item). Keyless CONTENTdm JSON API (/digital/api/search/collection/<alias>/searchterm/<term>/maxRecords/N; item detail /digital/api/collections/<alias>/items/<id>/false with imageUri/iiifInfoUri) and IIIF images, the same stack the probe verified cross-origin at UW (digitalcollections.lib.washington.edu, ACAO *, images ~700 px at IIIF level 1). WARNING: OCLC's redesigned CONTENTdm went live 22 Sep 2026 and a third-party note says the new version has no published public API; re-verify the /digital/api paths before relying on them. Renamed program 'Washington Digital Heritage' (2018); 2024-25 awardees include MOHAI, Jamestown S'Klallam, Quileute, Asotin County, Orcas/Lopez libraries. Reported size: 12,259 items (2012), 'more than 11,000' catalogued resources from 80+ institutions (undated); Northwest Digital Heritage (its DPLA hub) has 839k records across WA/OR/ID.
sources.coverage: Rural and small-town WA (North Central WA: Chelan, Douglas, Ferry, Grant, Okanogan; Whitman; Asotin; San Juans; many others); Seattle/Tacoma/Spokane are covered by their own library sites instead.
sources.license_terms: Per-item rights statements (many 'no known copyright' for pre-1930 local photos; some in-copyright); credit the contributing institution; check each item's rights field before display.
sources.example_request: Runtime (if the API survives the 2026 redesign): GET https://www.washingtonruralheritage.org/digital/api/search/collection/all/searchterm/<town>/field/all/mode/all/conn/and/maxRecords/12 ; else build-time harvest via OAI-PMH (https://www.washingtonruralheritage.org/oai/oai.php?verb=ListRecords&metadataPrefix=oai_dc&set=<alias>) into data/photos/<county>.json with only rights-cleared items. Alternative statewide aggregator with a stable API: DPLA (api.dp.la, free key, CORS) filtered to provider 'Northwest Digital Heritage' and state 'Washington'.
sources.size_or_volume: ~12k+ items; per-town hits typically tens to hundreds.
sources.notes: This is the best single source for 'a photo of this town around 1910' outside the big three cities.

sources.name: Regional library/museum photo archives for the other big cities (Tacoma, Spokane, Everett, Bellingham, Seattle Public Library)
sources.what_it_gives: Tacoma Public Library Northwest ORCA (AtoM-based, tpl.accesstomemory.org) with the Tacoma-Pierce County Buildings Index: address-keyed records with year built, style, demolished flag, register status, architects/builders/contractors, occupants with dates, drawn from Tacoma newspapers 1883-1963 and 200+ books (the single best 'history of this house' source outside King County). Spokane Public Library Ned M. Barnes Northwest Room: 2,000+ digital images (CONTENTdm-era; Spokane Fire 1889, bridges, Indian Congress, mining, rail). Everett Public Library Northwest Room digital collections (CONTENTdm; photos, maps, 1914 and 1955 Everett Sanborns; room closed for renovation through fall 2026). Whatcom Museum Photo Archives: 200,000 images (Darius Kinsey etc.) but only selections online, PastPerfect in-house, $1/MB for files. Seattle Public Library Special Collections (CONTENTdm cdm16118.contentdm.oclc.org, collection p15015coll4 'Seattle Historic Photograph Collection', Lenggenhager 4,800+ images 1950-84, Century 21, city directories).
sources.coverage: Tacoma/Pierce (buildings index, 1883-1963), Spokane, Everett/Snohomish, Bellingham/Whatcom, Seattle.
sources.license_terms: Per item; many pre-1930 photos marked no known copyright (Seattle PL items on DPLA carry 'No Copyright - United States'); Tacoma/Spokane library images free to view, reproduction rights per item; Whatcom Museum images require purchase/permission.
sources.example_request: Tacoma Buildings Index link-out by address (verify the live search URL; the 2015 handout gave search.tacomalibrary.org/buildings, now under Northwest ORCA): https://northwestroom.tacomalibrary.org/index.php/informationobject/browse?topLod=0&query="6226 S WARNER ST". Seattle PL CONTENTdm API: https://cdm16118.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/api/search/collection/p15015coll4/searchterm/<neighborhood>/maxRecords/12 (same post-Sep-2026 caveat).
sources.size_or_volume: Tacoma index: tens of thousands of addresses; Spokane 2k images; Seattle PL ~10 collections.
sources.notes: For Tacoma the Buildings Index is the house-ring equivalent of King County's YrBuilt extract; it is HTML-only (AtoM has an OAI-PMH endpoint and a JSON API in newer versions - check /api), so start with a link-out and consider a build-time OAI harvest later.

sources.name: Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer Data Mart weekly extracts (year built for Tacoma and Pierce County)
sources.what_it_gives: Zipped, pipe-delimited, header-less, ISO-8859-1 text tables refreshed weekly: tax_account, appraisal_account, improvement (parcel_number 10 digits + building_id; square feet, condition, quality, percent complete), improvement_builtas (parcel_number, building_id, built_as_number, built-as description, year built, stories, units, bedrooms, bathrooms per the ePIP building screen; the exact column name was not confirmable from the sandbox), improvement_detail, sale, land, tax_description; metadata PDFs per table at https://online.co.pierce.wa.us/cfapps/atr/datamart/metadata/<table>.pdf and a relationship diagram. Join to Pierce County Tax Parcels (gisdata-piercecowa.opendata.arcgis.com, TaxParcelNumber) for geometry.
sources.coverage: All of Pierce County (Tacoma, Puyallup, Lakewood, etc.), ~330k parcels; 'year built' as recorded by the assessor (effective year may differ after major remodels).
sources.license_terms: County public records; RCW 42.56.070(9) no-commercial-use-of-lists restriction as with King County; cite 'Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer'. Weekly refresh; county warns data may not be current.
sources.example_request: Build: download improvement_builtas.zip + improvement.zip; map columns using the metadata PDFs (no header row!); take min(year_built) per parcel_number; emit data/yrbuilt/53053/<first4digits>.json shards {parcel_number: year}. Runtime: Pierce parcel polygon (CORS * on ArcGIS Hub feature service) -> parcel number -> shard lookup.
sources.size_or_volume: improvement tables a few hundred MB unzipped; output ~3-4 MB sharded.
sources.notes: A GitHub project (multicare-parcel-mapping-2026) already scripts this download pipeline (scripts/build-pierce-assessor.mjs) and documents the no-header/encoding quirks; reuse its column maps after checking them against the PDFs.

sources.name: Snohomish County Assessor - Improvements Record + Assessor Roll CSV collection + Parcels feature layer (Open Data Portal)
sources.what_it_gives: 'Improvements Record' file (document download): parcel number, use code description, improvement type, year built, and other improvement features/dates (initial construction, renovations, additions). 'Assessor Roll CSV Collection' with five tables (MainData, NameAddr, SegMerge, Exemptions, LegalDescr) related by PropId/parcel_number. 'Parcels' feature layer (current boundaries, updated 3x/week, downloadable; avoid 'All Parcels (Past and Present)' for joins).
sources.coverage: All of Snohomish County (Everett, Lynnwood, Edmonds, Marysville...), ~300k parcels.
sources.license_terms: County open data; assessor files 'freely available'; no technical support; RCW 42.56.070(9) applies to name lists. Cite 'Snohomish County Assessor'.
sources.example_request: Build: download the Improvements Record (check the Hub item for CSV vs Access vs zip), keep parcel_number + min year built; shard as for Pierce. Runtime: Parcels FeatureServer point query (ArcGIS Hub -> services.arcgis.com, CORS *) -> PARCEL_ID -> shard.
sources.size_or_volume: Hundreds of thousands of improvement rows; output ~3 MB sharded.
sources.notes: Field names unverified from the sandbox; read the data dictionary linked from the Parcels dataset page during the first build.

sources.name: Spokane County - Assessor Parcels MapServer + parcel data file downloads (res_impr_info / comm_impr_info with year_built)
sources.what_it_gives: Downloadable assessor tables incl. res_impr_info (year_built text(4), eff_year_built, year_remodeled, ...) and comm_impr_info (year_built = year the improvement was constructed), keyed by county parcel number (data dictionary PDF 'County Data Table Description'); parcel polygons via https://gismo.spokanecounty.org/arcgis/rest/services/Assessor/Parcels/MapServer/0 (SR 2926, max 2000, JSON/GeoJSON/PBF) and the Hub parcel dataset; the DAHP County_Parcels service also mirrors Spokane parcels (display field PID). SCOUT is the public viewer (shows year built per lot).
sources.coverage: All of Spokane County incl. City of Spokane and Spokane Valley, ~210k parcels.
sources.license_terms: County open data (Hub) / public records; cite 'Spokane County Assessor'.
sources.example_request: Build: download res_impr_info + comm_impr_info, cast year_built to int, min per parcel; shard. Runtime: Hub 'Parcel' feature layer (services.arcgis.com, CORS *) point query -> PID -> shard; fall back to gismo MapServer if the Hub copy lacks fields.
sources.size_or_volume: ~250k improvement rows; output ~2 MB sharded.
sources.notes: Spokane's open data hub also publishes the City of Spokane's own GIS data (my.spokanecity.org/opendata/gis) incl. historic districts.

sources.name: Clark County (Vancouver WA) - Property Assessment and Taxation Data zip + GIS bulk download
sources.what_it_gives: Single zip of delimited text tables from the Assessor/Treasurer database: building table (style, improvements; year built expected but not confirmed in snippets), building summary view, land, sales, etc.; monthly shapefile bulk download incl. BuildingFootprints and taxlots; Hub feature services (GeoServices/WMS/WFS). Property Information Center (PIC) is the public viewer.
sources.coverage: All of Clark County, ~180k parcels.
sources.license_terms: County open data; cite 'Clark County Assessor'.
sources.example_request: Build: download the assessment zip, locate the building table, read its field list for a year-built column, min per parcel; shard. Runtime: Hub taxlot feature layer point query.
sources.size_or_volume: Tens of MB; output ~1.5 MB sharded.
sources.notes: Lower priority than Pierce/Snohomish/Spokane; the same pattern applies.

sources.name: Thurston, Kitsap, Whatcom, Yakima (and other counties) - assessor extracts and parcel layers (year built availability varies)
sources.what_it_gives: Thurston: Assessor's Property Table (APT/APTE) as Access database downloads with field docs; 'Thurston Parcels' open-data layer (131,392 records, custom license) from ASCEND/SIGMA; A+ parcel search shows Year Built. Kitsap: weekly tab-delimited Parcels, Dwellings, Land_detail text files with PDF descriptions (year built likely in Dwellings). Whatcom: 'Short Master' CSV/MDB/XLSX (parcel, address, owner, values; year built only in the Tax Parcel Viewer). Yakima: lookup tools (Assessor Parcel Search, Yakimap) only, no bulk year-built file found. Other counties: start from the statewide parcel layer's DATA_LINK field (per-county assessor URL).
sources.coverage: County by county; year built in bulk confirmed only partially (Kitsap Dwellings likely; Thurston APT likely; Whatcom/Yakima viewer-only).
sources.license_terms: County public records; Thurston parcels layer carries a custom license; RCW 42.56.070(9) list restriction; cite each county assessor.
sources.example_request: Build (per county, as budget allows): download the extract, confirm a year-built field in the data dictionary, shard by parcel id; otherwise emit only a link-out URL template for that county's parcel viewer.
sources.size_or_volume: Varies; each county's shards 0.5-2 MB.
sources.notes: Recommended rollout order by population and data quality: King (done), Pierce, Snohomish, Spokane, Clark, Thurston, Kitsap; all others link-out via DATA_LINK.

sources.name: Washington statewide Current Parcels (WA Geospatial Open Data Portal / OCIO) - parcel geometry + situs address for all 39 counties
sources.what_it_gives: Annual statewide compilation of county tax parcels (Parcels_2026, updated Apr 2026; previous years retained): FIPS_NR, COUNTY_NM, PARCEL_ID_NR, ORIG_PARCEL_ID, SITUS_ADDRESS, SUB_ADDRESS, SITUS_CITY_NM, SITUS_ZIP_NR, LANDUSE_CD (DOR land use code), VALUE_LAND, VALUE_BLDG, DATA_LINK (county assessor page URL), owner/taxpayer fields, Shape__Area; NO year built. Also mirrored as WA DNR 'County Tax Parcels' on gis.dnr.wa.gov/site2 (WADNR_PUBLIC_OCIO_Parcels/MapServer/0). The UW 'Washington State Parcel Database' (normalized attributes incl. YearBuilt in its development schema) is not hosted online (request-only, licensing gaps).
sources.coverage: All 39 counties, current year.
sources.license_terms: geo.wa.gov lists a custom license (view details on the item); owner names present (RCW 42.56.070(9)); use only for geometry/address/parcel id and DATA_LINK; cite 'Washington State Parcels, WA OCIO Geospatial Program'.
sources.example_request: GET https://services.arcgis.com/jsIt88o09Q0r1j8h/arcgis/rest/services/Current_Parcels/FeatureServer/0/query?geometry=-117.426,47.658&geometryType=esriGeometryPoint&inSR=4326&outFields=COUNTY_NM,PARCEL_ID_NR,SITUS_ADDRESS,LANDUSE_CD,DATA_LINK&returnGeometry=true&outSR=4326&f=geojson  (services.arcgis.com returns ACAO *; this one host gives the 'lot' ring statewide).
sources.size_or_volume: ~3.2M parcels; point query only.
sources.notes: Use this single service for the house/lot ring everywhere in WA; use county-specific services (King PropertyInfo, Seattle PARCEL_GEO) only where they add year built or extra attributes; the DATA_LINK gives the per-county 'see the assessor record' link for free.

sources.name: Ice-age extents: Dyke et al. 2003 'Deglaciation of North America' shapefiles (GitHub mirror), NADI-1 (Dalton et al. 2023, Zenodo), and WA DNR unit symbols as proxy
sources.what_it_gives: Dyke 2003 GSC Open File 1574: continental ice-margin/proglacial-lake polygons per time slice (radiocarbon years BP; folder WGS84 with one folder per slice iceXXXXXX) - the classic Cordilleran/Laurentide retreat maps. NADI-1 (Dalton et al. 2023): 49 time-steps 25-1 ka in calendar years with optimal/min/max margins as shapefiles (Zenodo doi 10.5281/zenodo.8161764); Dalton 2020 had 36 isochrones (QSR 234:106223 supplement). Regional detail for the Puget Lobe (max ~16,000-17,000 cal BP; Thorson 1980 ice-thickness contours shown on DNR's glacial geology page; Haugerud's lidar-based margin in his open-access GSA chapter, figure derived from Schuster 2010 / Haugerud & Tabor 2009) exists only as figures, not downloadable GIS.
sources.coverage: Continental scale (coarse at the Puget Lowland/Columbia Basin level); Missoula flood extents not included (use DNR Qfg/Qf* polygons; USGS/IAFI story maps for narrative; floods ~18,000-15,000 cal BP per NPS/DNR, DNR DMU text says 15,300-12,700).
sources.license_terms: Dyke 2003: Natural Resources Canada open file (Open Government Licence - Canada; cite Dyke, Moore & Robertson 2003). NADI-1 Zenodo: check record license (expected CC BY 4.0). DNR units: WGS free with credit.
sources.example_request: Build: clone awickert/North-American-Ice-Sheets (raw files reachable), take WGS84 slices for ~18, 16, 15, 14, 13, 12, 11, 10 ka (convert 14C to cal with IntCal), clip to WA bbox, simplify -> data/ice/<ka>.geojson (tens of KB each). Then override the Puget Lowland with a hand-digitized Vashon maximum polygon traced from DNR's Thorson map (cite it) for visual accuracy.
sources.size_or_volume: Dyke slices: a few hundred KB each clipped; NADI-1 zip tens of MB.
sources.notes: For the 'ice age' slider stop, the DNR surface-geology units already answer 'was this spot under ice / under flood water' at parcel resolution (Qgt/Qgo/Qga/Qgd... vs Qfg/Qfs...); use the continental polygons only to draw the ice front across the state map.

sources.name: Washington territorial/statehood chronology (curated from Wikipedia + HistoryLink; content for the 'Washington' ring)
sources.what_it_gives: Anchor dates to pre-bake into data/state/timeline.json: 1775 Heceta lands at Point Grenville; 1792 Vancouver surveys Puget Sound, Gray enters the Columbia (May 11); 1805-06 Lewis & Clark reach the Pacific; 1810-11 Spokane House, Fort Okanogan, Fort Astoria; 1818 Anglo-American joint occupation; 1819 Adams-Onis (Spain cedes claims); 1825 Fort Vancouver (HBC); 1833 Fort Nisqually; 1836 Whitman Mission; 1843 Oregon Provisional Government; 1845 Vancouver and Lewis counties created north of the Columbia; 15 Jun 1846 Oregon Treaty sets the 49th parallel; 1847 Whitman killings; 14 Aug 1848 Oregon Territory; 1850 Donation Land Claim Act; 13 Nov 1851 Denny Party at Alki; 1852 King/Pierce/Jefferson/Island/Thurston counties; 2 Mar 1853 Washington Territory (Isaac Stevens governor); Dec 1854-Jun 1855 Stevens treaties; 1855-56 Yakima and Puget Sound wars (Battle of Seattle 26 Jan 1856); 1858 Leschi executed; 14 Feb 1859 Oregon statehood enlarges WA Territory; 1859 Pig War; 3 Mar 1863 Idaho Territory split (Wikipedia says 4 Mar) fixing today's borders; 21 Oct 1872 San Juan award; 8 Sep 1883 Northern Pacific completed; 4 Jun/6 Jun/4 Jul/4 Aug 1889 fires (Seattle Jun 6, Ellensburg Jul 4, Spokane Aug 4); 11 Nov 1889 statehood (42nd state); 1897 Klondike; 1899 Mount Rainier NP; 1909 AYP Exposition; 1910 women's suffrage; 1 Mar 1911 Pend Oreille County (last); 1917 Ballard Locks; 1919 Seattle General Strike; 1940 Tacoma Narrows collapse; 1942 Japanese American removal; 1942 Grand Coulee; 1943 Hanford; 1962 World's Fair; 18 May 1980 Mount St. Helens; 28 Feb 2001 Nisqually quake. Deep-time stops: 26 Jan 1700 Cascadia M9; ~900-930 CE Seattle Fault quake; ~5,600 BP Osceola Mudflow; ~7,700 BP Mazama ash; 18-15 ka Missoula floods; ~17-16 ka Vashon ice maximum; 17-6 Ma Columbia River Basalts; ~50 Ma Siletzia accretion; ~100 Ma North Cascades terrane assembly; ~1.4 Ga Belt Supergroup (NE WA).
sources.coverage: Statewide political/geologic chronology; the build script should re-verify each date against the linked Wikipedia/HistoryLink page and store the source URL.
sources.license_terms: Facts; attribute Wikipedia (CC BY-SA) and HistoryLink (link-only) per entry.
sources.example_request: data/state/timeline.json: [{"date":"1853-03-02","title":"Washington Territory organized","ring":"state","src":"https://www.historylink.org/file/5210"}, ...]; the time control picks entries with date <= selected date for each ring.
sources.size_or_volume: ~80 state entries; city timelines from Wikipedia 'Timeline of Seattle' and 'Timeline of Spokane, Washington' (no 'Timeline of Tacoma' article exists; use the Tacoma article's history section and HistoryLink 5055/20749).
sources.notes: Wikipedia 'Timeline of X' articles are year-keyed bullet lists ideal for the city ring; parse at build time with the API (prose is CC BY-SA, so store short paraphrases + links, not verbatim bullets).

gaps: 1. City incorporation dates: no single machine-readable statewide list exists (OFM/AWC/SoS publish none); must be assembled from Wikipedia city infoboxes, MRSC profiles and HistoryLink essays, and the legal 'date' (vote vs. order vs. SoS filing) is ambiguous for older towns. Whether the Wikipedia municipalities list table has an 'Incorporated' column was not verifiable here. 2. Historical populations before 1890 for cities exist only via Wikipedia infoboxes / CESTA (rounded, sparse: 1870 x8, 1880 x19 WA places) and the Census volumes themselves; the Census API is useless (key, no pre-2000, no CORS); Wikidata P1082/P585 series are absent for almost all WA towns. 3. Pierce County year-built column name and the Snohomish/Clark/Thurston/Kitsap field names were not confirmable (hosts blocked); each needs one look at the data dictionary during the first build. No statewide year-built layer exists (geo.wa.gov parcels lack it; UW's normalized DB is offline), so year built stays county-by-county. 4. Newberry license is internally contradictory (CC BY-NC-SA deed in zip vs 'any lawful purpose' page vs CC0 by email); fine for this free site but should be noted in the credits. 5. OHM: county boundaries statewide now come from the Newberry import but a known chronology start_date bug exists; outside Seattle, OHM Washington is nearly empty (Spokane 413 dated ways, Tacoma 79, other cities ~0), and the 1936 Seattle street import gives artificial 1936 start dates. 6. No dated ice-margin or Missoula-flood GIS exists at Puget-Lowland resolution (only continental Dyke/NADI-1 polygons and figures in papers); the DNR map units are the practical proxy. 7. No 'regions of Washington' official layer; use EPA ecoregions or a hand-made county->region table. 8. Esri's historical-topo ImageServer is governed by the Esri MLA and could require tokens later; the public-domain path (USGS GeoTIFFs -> self-hosted PMTiles) costs build effort and repo size. 9. CONTENTdm's Sept 2026 redesign may have removed the keyless JSON API used by Washington Rural Heritage, Seattle PL, Everett PL and UW; needs a live check, with OAI-PMH or DPLA as fallbacks. 10. WA State Archives, WSHS, HistoryLink, Washington Digital Newspapers, Tacoma Buildings Index and BLM GLO are link-out only (no APIs; GLO bulk CSVs withdrawn 2022). 11. Volcanic_Vents layer fields, DAHP inventory current schema and CORS for wisaard/EPA/USFS/NPS/gismo hosts are unverified (all are build-time-safe regardless). 12. Chronicling America's post-Aug-2025 loc.gov endpoints were not CORS-tested (www.loc.gov returned ACAO * in the probe, so it is likely fine). 13. Exact LOC Sanborn statewide count and the sanborn09nnn id range for WA need one build-time query to pin down.
recommendation: Design the statewide rings around a small set of pre-baked JSON files plus three runtime hosts (services.arcgis.com for parcels, gis.dnr.wa.gov for geology/PLSS, loc.gov for maps/newspapers), everything else link-out. Build script (GitHub Actions, run monthly, commits data/): (a) counties: Newberry WA shapefile -> data/counties/versions.json (dated polygons, simplified) + chronology.json; Newberry states/territories (0.01 deg) -> territory_versions.json; join Wikipedia county list (Est., Origin, seat) and county infobox populations 1860-2020, NBER/Forstall as tiebreaker, HistoryLink county essay ids (via the Wikidata 'HistoryLink essay number' property resolved by label, then the Thumbnail History Index File 9143). (b) places: Wikipedia municipalities list + city infoboxes (incorporation dates, {{US Census population}}), OFM 1890-2020 Excel (authoritative counts), CESTA/CreatingData CSVs (public-domain fill for 1860-1880), MRSC profiles for missing dates, Wikidata QIDs/coords, HistoryLink city and Seattle-neighborhood essay ids -> data/places/municipalities.json + pops.json + historylink.json. (c) regions: EPA Level III ecoregions clipped to WA + hand-written regions.json (region name, counties, deep-time blurb). (d) pre-1850 and treaty layers: USFS Royce cessions clipped to WA (public domain) and Native Land territories (key in an Actions secret, unmodified polygons, their disclaimer). (e) maps: HTMC WA index (4,594 sheets, 1894-2005) -> compact topo index with thumbnails and GeoTIFF links; a curated dozen early sheets (Seattle 1897/1909, Tacoma, Spokane, Olympia, Walla Walla, Bellingham, Vancouver, Yakima) warped and tiled to PMTiles in the repo so the historical-map layer never depends on Esri; LOC Sanborn WA item index; NRHP WA points; DAHP register properties (if license text allows) or link-out. (f) year built: King County extracts (probe) sharded by Major prefix; then Pierce, Snohomish, Spokane, Clark in that order, each as parcel-id -> year shards (~2-4 MB per county) loaded lazily; all other counties fall back to the statewide parcel layer's DATA_LINK. (g) timelines: state timeline.json (verified anchor dates), city timelines parsed from Wikipedia 'Timeline of Seattle'/'Timeline of Spokane' as short paraphrases with links, HistoryLink census-year essays per decade. Runtime per visit: one statewide-parcel point query (lot ring, address, DATA_LINK), Seattle/King overlays where available, DNR layer-11 + table-13 lookups (or pre-baked DMU), DNR PLSS section, point-in-polygon against the pre-baked county versions/territories/regions/cessions/ecoregions for the selected date, Esri exportImage or PMTiles for the map, LOC Chronicling America and Sanborn links for the selected year, Overpass only for Seattle-level OHM detail. Licensing: everything in-page is public domain, CC0, CC BY or state-agency free-with-credit; HistoryLink (CC BY-NC-ND), WSHS, WA Archives, Washington Digital Newspapers, Tacoma Buildings Index and BLM GLO stay as credited links. Put a single credits.json behind an 'About the data' page listing Newberry, OHM, WGS/DNR, USGS, LOC, OFM, Census/CESTA, Wikipedia/Wikidata, HistoryLink, DAHP, NPS, USFS, Native Land, EPA and each county assessor. First-build verification checklist: confirm the Wikipedia municipalities table columns, Pierce improvement_builtas column order, CONTENTdm API survival, loc.gov CORS on the chronicling-america path, the OHM Newberry id tag key, and the LOC sanborn09 id range.
